items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Danny Doris, the vibraphonist with whom I had worked quite a few times.

ctx.x: After Super-Besse, we went to Nice where we got a taste of spring, then in April, we went to Morocco to Meknes, Rabat and Casablanca. It had been very long time since my last trip there. This time, I was playing with a band directed by Jacques Largeaud, who played organ and piano. He was also a school teacher, and was very nice and interesting fellow and we had a swell time. A few weeks laterm I went back to Copenhagen to do a T.V.show with Teddy Wilson. The funny thing is that we flew in the same plane and did…

I went back to play at the Trois Mailletz. I had been angry for some time with Madame Calvé, but decided to forget the difference. Past was past, and it's nice sometimes to play in a club. Another club where I started to play was the Caveau de la Huchette, also situated in the Latin Quarter, which had been bought by Danny Doris, the vibraphonist with whom I had worked quite a few times. The atmosphere of the Huchette was more easier going than at the Trois Mailletz, where people came more to listen to music. In…

A famous well known French composer and singer, Guy Béart, contacted me. He had a T.V. programme called "Bienvenue" which means "Welcome" to Guy Béart. He wss having that programme about twice a month, andhe was inviting all kinds of personalities for his show. He told me that he wanted to make a show called "Bienvenue to American artists", and asked me if I was willing to contact the American musicians available in Paris. I rang Mickey Baker, guitarist, Kenny Clark, drummer, Art Simmons, piano, Benny Water,…
